text:
alex: Heads up — noticed a p95 latency bump on the continuous batcher during the 11:00 deploy, looks tied to kernel selection churn.
jana: saw the alert, can you paste the profiler output?
alex: perf-bot flagged it first: `perf-bot: alert p95+18% (long-seq requests) - region-us-west2`
alex: from sampling, we pick FlashAttention for many shards, but when paged-KV residency is low we get page faults and token shed. kernel_switch_count spikes in the same window.
rico: that makes sense. FlashAttn is great for big contiguous KV, but if paged KV causes misses the kernel handoff is costly. what's our eligibility window and token budget right now?
alex: current settings: `eligibility_window_ms=25`, `token_budget_per_batch=2048`, `max_seq_len_probe=4096` — in practice long sequences wait and pull in small tails, bloating batch token counts.
anya: telemetry shows median batch token size up 12% and token_latency variance doubled. Also increased KV pagefault rate from 0.2% -> 1.9% for the affected fleet.
jana: quick hypothesis: wide eligibility window + aggressive kernel preference for FlashAttn => batches accumulate mixed residency states and then FlashAttn loses efficiency, fallback cost climbs.
rico: short-term fix: narrow the eligibility window to 8-12ms to reduce mixed-residency batches. also bias kernel selector: if paged_kv_residency < 0.7 prefer fallback-attn for that batch.
alex: agree. propose canary: set eligibility_window_ms=10 and add selector rule `if paged_kv_miss_rate>0.5% then prefer_fallback=true` on 3 nodes in us-west2 for 1 hour.
perf-bot: scheduled canary: config change pushed to fleet-canary-3 (us-west2) — will report p95/kv-miss in 15m windows.
anya: if the canary improves p95 by >10% without throughput loss, open a rollout RFC. Also add a metric: `kernel_handoff_latency` to trace points.
jana: also add a short profiler capture (2%) with seq-length tagging so we can confirm which sequences trigger the handoff.
alex: I'll open a PR with the config tweak and attach the profiler command. doing the capture now.
rico: if canary looks good, follow up with a scheduler-level improvement: prefer co-located-residency batching (sticky prefix matching) before widening eligibility.
alex: noted. thanks all — will post results in ~20m.
perf-bot: canary update (15m): p95 down 11%, kv-miss down to 0.6%, kernel_handoff_latency down 30% on canary nodes.
alex: excellent. starting rollout RFC draft and tagging eng-runtime ops for a staged rollout.
jana: thumbs up :thumbsup:
file_notes: continuous batching tuning convo, kernel selection + paged KV canary
